bookCredit: Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of NIMH (Robert C. O’Brien, 1971), Number the Stars (Lois Lowry, 1989), Freedom Train (Dorothy Sterling, 1954) and Prince Caspian (C. S. Lewis, 1951) are quoted only in short lines. Anne of Green Gables (L. M. Montgomery, 1908) is in the public domain.
title: The Reader You Are Now

banner.alt: A gallery at dawn with five pedestals in a row, a reading lamp, a rocking chair, and an owl on the sill

keepsake.name: owl feather
keepsake.line: Only Imagination Trip travelers earn this one. Opti left it on the last pedestal, for the reader you are now.

body: A mouse, a carpet bag, a lunch basket, a quilt, and a lion. You read all five this year, and you are not the same reader who opened the first one.
Build a gallery of your year, in order.
postcard.word: To reflect means to think back on something and what it taught you.

mission.h: Build the gallery of your reading year
mission.p: Five pedestals in reading order, one object from each book, your chair at the end.

steps.build:
Open your menu (top button, right controller) and click Models. Build in this order:
  1. five pedestals in a row
  2. on them, in reading order: mouse, carpet bag, basket, quilt, lion
  3. at the end: a pencil, for the reader you are now
steps.say: Walk the row from first to last. Practice these 2 sentences:
steps.frame: “In August I ___. Now I ___, and my proof is ___.”
steps.extra: Put a Rocking Chair (Optima Domi) past the last pedestal: your reading chair.

points: Your video is 30 seconds or less, shows the five pedestals in order with the pencil at the end, and you say 2 sentences: who you were as a reader in August, who you are now, and one moment from a book as proof.

alt.p: Match each book you read this year to one thing you remember from it.
alt.gameH: Tap a book, then tap what belongs to it

pairs.a: Mrs. Frisby and the Rats of NIMH
pairs.b: a mother mouse with a house to move
pairs.why: The first book of the year, back in August.

pairs.b: a plain road renamed the White Way of Delight
pairs.why: Anne gave the prettiest places better names on her first drive.

pairs.b: a lunch basket with a packet under the napkin
pairs.why: Annemarie carried it past the soldiers to Uncle Henrik’s boat.

pairs.b: a quilt pieced from scraps, the household’s only treasure
pairs.why: Old Rit sewed it by firelight. Harriet left it on a doorstep as thank you and farewell.

pairs.b: a horn that brings help when it is blown
pairs.why: Queen Susan’s horn, blown between nine and ten of the clock, pulled four children off a railway platform.

pairs.b: not the same reader who opened the first book
pairs.why: That is the whole point of this week. Find the moment it changed.

alt.miss: Not that one. Think about which book that thing came from.

write.q: Who were you as a reader in August, and who are you now? In 2 sentences, say what changed and give one moment from one of the five books as proof.
starters: My proof is the moment when ___.

scripts.brief: Hoo there, it’s Opti. A mouse, a girl with a carpet bag, a lunch basket, a patchwork quilt, and a lion. You read all five books this year, and you are not the same reader who opened the first one. Build a gallery of your year in reading order, one object from each book, and stand at the end. Then tell me who you were in August and who you are now.
scripts.alt: No headset? Take the window seat with me one last time. Five books on one shelf, and one more thing on it: you. Match each book to something you remember from it, and notice how much you carry now.
scripts.saved: The gallery is built, first book to last, and the pencil is waiting at the end. Here is your owl feather. Keep it, and remember that stories become part of who you are.

testPara: In August I read slowly and skipped the hard words. Now I read with a pencil in my hand, and my proof is the moment when I worked out what Papa's cigarettes meant in Number the Stars before Annemarie did.
